sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusables and KG hints, Speed, slow driving and signaling

FACT_ID: sec09-R01 | anchor: A01
The interstate designated limit is seventy miles per hour, while an open county highway is limited to fifty-five miles per hour, each unless otherwise posted [A01].
Why it matters: group speed-limits; difficulty medium; prereq sec09-F05; confusables sec09-F05 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-R02 | anchor: A01
Business and residential areas carry a twenty-five miles per hour limit, but a school zone drops to fifteen miles per hour while children are present along the roadway [A01].
Why it matters: group speed-limits; difficulty medium; prereq sec09-F05; confusables sec09-F05, sec09-F06 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-R03 | anchor: A01
A posted limit is a ceiling, not a target, because driving faster than is reasonable and prudent for the conditions is illegal even below the posted number [A01].
Why it matters: group basic-speed-law; difficulty medium; prereq sec09-F04; confusables sec09-F01, sec09-F04 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-R04 | anchor: A02
A slow driver keeps as far right as possible, and on a road with one lane each way and no clear passing lane must pull off at the first safe turnout to let faster traffic by [A02].
Why it matters: group slow-driving; difficulty medium; prereq sec09-F09; confusables sec09-F09, sec09-F10 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec09-R05 | anchor: A02
A turn signal is required at least one hundred feet before the turn, yet for a turn just past an intersection signaling too early misleads other drivers as surely as signaling too late [A02].
Why it matters: group signaling; difficulty high; prereq sec09-F13; confusables sec09-F13, sec09-F14 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec09-R06 | anchor: A02
An arm pointing down signals slowing or stopping, an arm pointing up signals a right turn, and an arm straight out signals a left turn [A02].
Why it matters: group hand-signals; difficulty high; prereq sec09-F15; confusables sec09-F15 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec09-R07 | anchor: A01
Only an authorized emergency vehicle on emergency duty with its signal equipment operating may exceed the posted limit, and even then only without endangering other road users [A01].
Why it matters: group emergency-vehicles; difficulty low; prereq sec09-F07; confusables sec09-F07, sec09-F04 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-R08 | anchor: A02
The recommended grip puts the left hand near eight o'clock and the right hand near four o'clock on the wheel, a low position chosen partly because of the air bag [A02].
Why it matters: group vehicle-control; difficulty low; prereq sec09-F16; confusables sec09-F16 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0053]
